yt_title: A Perfect Bracket Would Take 25 Quadrillion Years
yt_description:
How long would it take to get a perfect March Madness bracket if you tried once a day? About 25 quadrillion years, roughly 1.8 million times the age of the universe. We ranked 8 rare odds by how long you'd wait at one try per day, from double sixes (about 5 weeks) to a royal flush (1,779 years) to a monkey typing "banana" (845,800 years).

How it works: on average, something with odds of 1 in N takes N tries, so at one try a day it takes N days.

0:44 Guessing a phone number
0:50 A perfect bracket

Sources: dice, card and combinatorics math; National Hole-in-One Registry via PGA.com; age of the universe 13.8 billion years (NASA); perfect bracket = 2^63 assuming every game is a coin flip.
